plan.title: HFD vs chow mouse liver DE + Hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 mouse liver RNA-seq samples (6 high-fat diet vs 6 chow, unpaired, single batch) supplied as pre-summed gene-level Salmon counts (12000 genes x 13 columns, gene symbols) plus a condition metadata table, with one flagged concern: sample_01's library size is ~4x below the median. The plan answers 'which genes and which pathways change' in four stages. First, sample-structure QC (blind vst, PCA on top-500 variable genes, distance heatmap, library sizes) verifies grouping by condition and inspects the shallow sample rather than silently dropping it — DESeq2's size factor down-weights it, so removal is a judgment with a stated reason, not a default. Second, the primary DE test: a minimal 10-count-in-6-samples pre-filter, DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering. A limitation is stated up front: because the input is already gene-summed counts with no transcript-level files, the tximport length-offset correction Salmon-derived counts would normally get cannot be applied and the report says so. Third, an edgeR quasi-likelihood run on the same filtered gene set provides the two-method robustness check; the intersection is the high-confidence DE set and method-only genes are reported as secondary, never the union. Fourth, fgsea preranked enrichment of the full tested list ranked by the Wald statistic (stated choice of the disputed metric) against the mouse-native MSigDB Hallmark (2026.1) and WikiPathways mouse (2026.07.10) collections — no human sets with a symbol remap on mouse data — with 15-500 member window, BH within each collection, and leading-edge genes per significant set. A final report consolidates the gene table (unshrunken + apeglm-shrunken log2FC + lfcSE), MA and dispersion plots, the p-value histogram checked before adjustment, the two-method overlap, the enrichment tables with collection releases and the method-dependence caveat, and a reproducibility record. Counts are small (12000 x 13), so every step is lightweight.

Median-of-ratios size factors computed and reported per sample (sample_01's factor visible)
Genes removed by pre-filter counted; p-value histogram inspected and its shape reported before BH adjustment
Number of genes tested after independent filtering, number of NA p-values from Cook's-distance outlier flagging, and number of DE genes (padj < 0.05) reported

reference level: explicitly set the condition factor reference to chow before fitting; contrast = condition, numerator HFD, denominator chow (vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0)

shrinkage: apeglm via lfcShrink (doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bty895)

multiple testing: BH at alpha=0.05 with independent filtering, alpha passed to results() matching the reporting cutoff; inspect the unadjusted p-value histogram before trusting adjusted p-values (doi:10.3390/ht7030023)

plan.title: HFD vs chow mouse liver DE + Hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 mouse liver RNA-seq samples (6 high-fat diet vs 6 chow, unpaired, single batch) supplied as pre-summed gene-level Salmon counts (12000 genes x 13 columns, gene symbols) plus a condition metadata table, with one flagged concern: sample_01's library size is ~4x below the median. The plan answers 'which genes and which pathways change' in four stages. First, sample-structure QC (blind vst, PCA on top-500 variable genes, distance heatmap, library sizes) verifies grouping by condition and inspects the shallow sample rather than silently dropping it — DESeq2's size factor down-weights it, so removal is a judgment with a stated reason, not a default. Second, the primary DE test: a minimal 10-count-in-6-samples pre-filter, DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering. A limitation is stated up front: because the input is already gene-summed counts with no transcript-level files, the tximport length-offset correction Salmon-derived counts would normally get cannot be applied and the report says so. Third, an edgeR quasi-likelihood run on the same filtered gene set provides the two-method robustness check; the intersection is the high-confidence DE set and method-only genes are reported as secondary, never the union. Fourth, fgsea preranked enrichment of the full tested list ranked by the Wald statistic (stated choice of the disputed metric) against the mouse-native MSigDB Hallmark (2026.1) and WikiPathways mouse (2026.07.10) collections — no human sets with a symbol remap on mouse data — with 15-500 member window, BH within each collection, and leading-edge genes per significant set. A final report consolidates the gene table (unshrunken + apeglm-shrunken log2FC + lfcSE), MA and dispersion plots, the p-value histogram checked before adjustment, the two-method overlap, the enrichment tables with collection releases and the method-dependence caveat, and a reproducibility record. Counts are small (12000 x 13), so every step is lightweight.
